body.p: . New part src/function_library_temporal.c (test function_library_temporal): adjust-dateTime/date/time-to- timezone, civil-timezone, days-in-month, parts-of-dateTime, build-dateTime, seconds, duration-to-seconds, unix-dateTime and parse-ietf-date. src/operator_temporal.c is unchanged.

item.p: Gregorian components (PR 1481): the seven *-from-dateTime rows of src/function_library_context.c (2.12's file, edited because no other packet runs on it; two hunks) take the union of the eight Gregorian types and give the empty sequence for a component the type lacks (absent components are zero in the datum).

Shifts: a dateTime or date moves by whole minutes through sxml_operator_make_temporal_value (: every int64_t year, FODT0001 beyond); a time moves within its day. The implicit timezone and the clock come from the dynamic context, read once per evaluation ().

build-dateTime declares map(*)?: the row text cannot spell the record's optional fields, so the body coerces each field by XPath 4.0, 3.4.3: xs:untypedAtomic cast, an integral xs:decimal relabeled to xs:integer, xs:double/xs:float cast to xs:decimal (seconds only), an xs:duration without months relabeled to xs:dayTimeDuration; other types, extra keys or two items are XPTY0004. Then FODT0005 (field set), FORG0001 (ranges, gMonthDay against 1972), FODT0003 (timezone). parts-of-dateTime returns a plain map with the record's keys in order.

Seconds keep nine fraction digits, truncated like casts (), so seconds(3.14159265358979323846) eq xs:dayTimeDuration('PT3.14159265358979323846S'); fn:seconds builds the duration from the decimal's digits (FODT0002 beyond int64_t seconds), not by duration arithmetic, which rounds.
unix-dateTime: milliseconds beyond uint64_t are FODT0001.

civil-timezone (, no database): no place gives the implicit timezone (the default place is taken to be one whose civil timezone it is); "UTC", "Etc/UTC", "GMT", "Etc/GMT" give PT0S; any other place FODT0004.

parse-ietf-date: hand-written scanner of the grammar of 9.10.1 (), ASCII case-insensitive, longest names first; a tzoffset of one to four digits is H, HH, HMM, HHMM, with a colon minutes are 0 or 2 digits; hour 24 only as 24:00:00 (next day); FORG0010 otherwise.
Open: fn-parts-of-dateTime 8/20 (assert-type needs the named record type, Proposed); civil-timezone 4/9 (); days-in-month-006/007 need fn:format-integer (2.9).
